newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech govt party sets confidence vote conditions.
newsitem.headline: Czech govt party sets confidence vote conditions.

text.p: A junior party in the Czech centre-right ruling coalition said on Friday that its support for the cabinet in a parliamentary confidence vote next week depended on further details of government austerity measures.

The reticence of the Christian Democratic Union (KDU-CSL), the most centrist of the three coalition parties, comes as the unpopular government struggles to implement an emergency plan to stabilise the currency, the crown, which has been under attack.

"I am confident our deputies will support the government in the confidence vote, but there are certain conditions that have to be fulfilled before they will be able to do so," KDU-CSL chairman and vice-premier Josef Lux told a news conference.
"First of all, the deputies will have to vote not for the people in the government, but for a concrete recovery programme the cabinet will present before the vote," Lux said.

Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus's government, which has seen its popularity plummet as the crown has lost more than 15 percent of its value in recent months, said it would call for the confidence vote as early as Tuesday.

The government austerity programme is aimed at slowing domestic demand and counteracting the inflationary effects of the crown's recent fall with sharp spending cuts leading to a balanced budget in 1997 and a budget surplus in 1998.
But the ministers have yet to detail the extent of the cuts, agreed in principle by coalition leaders last week.

Lux conceded it was necessary to take restrictive measures including a delay in pension and social payment increases "to boost our economy and help the central bank in its struggle for a stable currency". But he said deregulation of state-controlled energy and housing rents should be postponed.

The idea of postponing the deregulation steps -- which were agreed by the coalition parties in tense talks earlier this year -- is likely to meet stiff opposition from the KDU-CSL's two more right-wing partners
Lux said further talks on concrete steps in the programme would be needed in an extraordinary cabinet session on Monday.
"We (KDU-CSL) are confident that the government can fulfil its stabilisation and recovery programme. If we were not we would have already left the coalition," Lux said.
Lux's party appears to be the only waverer within the coalition, which holds 100 seats in the 200-seat lower house.

A government win, which requires a simple majority, may hinge on two independent deputies who are former members of the opposition Social Democratic party and whose voting intentions are unclear. The remaining 98 opposition deputies are expected to vote unanimously against the coalition.

Speaking on Reuters Financial Television, Ivan Pilip, the former education minister who replaced Ivan Kocarnik as finance minister last week, said if the cabinet won the vote, it would have room to implement its difficult plans.

"Next week on Tuesday there should be a confidence vote and we think that if we pass as a reconstructed government, that there is more space for some further steps concerning also the Czech crown because it plays a very important role," Pilip said.
